pageCache.text:
Our Ethos - The Grafton Way
Grafton believes that great education changes the trajectory of a child's life.
– Andrew Turnock, Headteacher
At Grafton Primary School, we believe education breaks cycles of disadvantage, gives children pathways they may not yet see, prepares them to make better choices, and equips them to improve not only their own lives, but the lives of others.
It is about far more than preparing children for the next stage of school. It is about preparing them for life.
A simple belief guides every decision we make: when children feel safe, valued and understood, they develop the confidence to learn, the courage to embrace new challenges and the resilience to thrive in an ever-changing world.
That is why everything we do is built around one promise:
Every child is known. Every child belongs. Every child is encouraged to flourish.
A Calm Place to Learn
Children learn best when they feel secure.
Our school is deliberately calm, structured and purposeful because we know that clear routines and consistent expectations help every child feel safe, confident and ready to learn. This is particularly important for children who may have experienced challenge, uncertainty or disruption in other areas of their lives.
A calm environment allows children to think deeply, concentrate fully and develop the independence they need to succeed.
Love and High Expectations
We believe that kindness and high expectations go hand in hand.
Caring for children means believing in what they can achieve. It means encouraging them when learning is difficult, celebrating their successes and supporting them when they make mistakes. It also means helping them understand that respect, responsibility and effort matter.
We expect children to work hard because we believe in their potential. We expect them to be kind because relationships matter. We expect them to persevere because resilience is built through challenge.
Our expectations are high because our belief in our children is even firmer.
Preparing Children for Life
Academic success is important, but it is only one part of education.
We want children to leave Grafton with the knowledge, confidence and character to make positive choices throughout their lives.
To believe that education opens doors.
To recognise that challenges can be overcome.
Our Values in Action
Our six values are not simply displayed on classroom walls. They are lived every day through the way we learn, work and care for one another.
A Community That Cares
Great schools are built on strong relationships.
We work closely with families because we know that children flourish when home and school work together.
We celebrate success together, support one another through challenges and create a community where everyone feels welcomed, respected and valued.
Our staff care deeply about every child. They know that education is not simply about teaching lessons — it is about building confidence, nurturing potential and helping children become the very best version of themselves.
Our Vision
When children leave Grafton Primary School, we hope they take far more than knowledge with them. We hope they leave -
Most of all, we hope they leave ready not only for secondary school, but for the opportunities, responsibilities and adventures that life will bring.
Because that is, and always will be, The Grafton Way.
With curiosity.
With confidence.
With kindness.
With resilience.
With creativity.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Grafton
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will make as a family. Whether you are discovering Grafton for the first time or are already part of our community, I hope this website gives you a real sense of who we are, what we value and what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow.
At Grafton, we believe every child deserves to be known, valued and encouraged to flourish. Children arrive with different experiences, talents and aspirations, and it is our privilege to help each one discover their strengths, develop confidence and enjoy learning.
Our six values — Love, Creativity, Kindness, Inclusion, Resilience and Empowerment — are at the heart of everything we do. They shape our classrooms, our relationships and the opportunities we provide, creating a school where children feel safe to ask questions, embrace challenges, celebrate success and learn from mistakes.
We are proud of our rich and diverse community. Every child brings something unique to Grafton, and we believe that learning alongside people from different backgrounds, cultures and experiences prepares children not only for secondary school, but for life. It teaches empathy, respect and an understanding that our differences make us stronger together.
Our curriculum is ambitious, broad and engaging. We want children to become confident readers, thoughtful mathematicians, curious scientists, creative artists, accomplished musicians, enthusiastic sportspeople and responsible digital citizens. More importantly, we want them to leave us as kind, resilient and compassionate young people who believe in themselves and in the positive difference they can make in the world.
None of this happens by chance. It is made possible by a dedicated team of staff who care deeply about every child in our school. We have high expectations because we believe in our children and we work tirelessly to ensure that learning is challenging, enjoyable and accessible to all, so that every child experiences success and develops a lifelong love of learning.
If you are considering Grafton for your child, I encourage you to explore our website, discover our curriculum, meet our subject leaders and learn more about the experiences that make life at Grafton so enriching. Better still, come and visit us. Nothing compares to seeing our school in action, meeting our children and experiencing the warmth, energy and sense of belonging that define our community.
If you are already part of the Grafton community, I hope you will find this website a helpful source of information and a window into the wonderful learning, achievements and experiences that your children enjoy every day.
Thank you for visiting our website. We look forward to welcoming you to Grafton Primary School.

pageCache.pageTitle: Grafton Primary School - Personal, Social & Health Education (PSHE)
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social & Health Education (PSHE)
At Grafton Primary School, we believe education is about far more than academic success. It is about helping children understand themselves, care for others and develop the confidence to make thoughtful, informed choices throughout their lives.
Our PSHE curriculum prepares children not just for the next year group, but for life beyond primary school. Through discussion, reflection and real-life situations, children learn how to build healthy relationships, manage emotions, keep themselves safe and become active, responsible members of their community.
Above all, PSHE gives children something incredibly important: the confidence to understand themselves and the world around them.
Preparing Children for Life
PSHE is woven through everyday life at Grafton.
It helps children develop the knowledge, skills and values they need to navigate an increasingly complex world with confidence, kindness and resilience. From understanding friendships and managing emotions to recognising unsafe situations, celebrating diversity and making healthy choices, children are gradually equipped with the tools they need to thrive.
Learning is carefully planned so that ideas are introduced at the right time and revisited as children mature, allowing understanding to deepen year by year.
Every Child Has a Voice
One of the greatest strengths of PSHE is that every child has the opportunity to be heard.
Lessons are discussion-rich, practical and engaging. Children learn through conversation, role play, collaborative activities, problem-solving and real-life scenarios rather than simply completing worksheets. This encourages children to think critically, listen respectfully to different viewpoints and express their own ideas with growing confidence.
By creating a safe and supportive classroom environment, we help children develop the confidence to ask questions, share opinions and learn from one another.
Relationships, Health and Wellbeing
Relationships and Sex Education (RSE) forms part of our wider PSHE curriculum and is taught in an age-appropriate, sensitive and inclusive way.
Our aim is to help children develop healthy relationships, understand their emotions, respect themselves and others and recognise how to keep themselves safe, both offline and online. Lessons also prepare children for growing up by introducing topics such as puberty, personal boundaries and body changes with care, accuracy and sensitivity.
Throughout the curriculum, we promote empathy, respect, inclusion and an appreciation of the many different families, communities and experiences that make up modern Britain.
Learning Beyond the Classroom
PSHE is not confined to one lesson each week.
Children apply their learning every day through opportunities to work together, solve problems and take responsibility within the wider school community.
A wonderful example of this is our Playground Friends programme. Older pupils organise games, welcome younger children into activities and help everyone feel included during playtimes. These experiences develop leadership, empathy and confidence while strengthening friendships across year groups. As children take ownership of these roles, they learn that leadership is about kindness, responsibility and helping others to belong.
Preparing Children for the Modern World
Children today are growing up in a world that changes rapidly.
Our curriculum helps them understand the opportunities and challenges they may encounter, including online safety, artificial intelligence, healthy relationships, stereotypes, mental health, consent, boundaries and personal wellbeing. Learning is continually reviewed and updated to reflect emerging issues and national guidance, ensuring it remains relevant, responsive and meaningful.
Rather than teaching children what to think, we teach them how to think critically, ask questions and make thoughtful decisions.
An Inclusive Curriculum
Every child deserves to see themselves reflected in what they learn.
Our PSHE curriculum celebrates diversity, promotes equality and ensures that every child feels respected, valued and included. Lessons are adapted where needed so that all learners, including those with SEND, can participate fully and confidently.
We believe children flourish when they feel accepted for who they are and are encouraged to appreciate the experiences and perspectives of others.
PSHE Through Our Values
Everything we teach in PSHE reflects the values that shape life at Grafton Primary School.
Love – Building positive relationships, caring for ourselves and showing compassion towards others.
Creativity – Exploring ideas through discussion, role play, problem-solving and collaborative learning.
Kindness – Developing empathy, understanding different perspectives and learning how our actions affect others.
Inclusion – Celebrating diversity and ensuring every child feels heard, respected and valued.
Resilience – Helping children manage emotions, overcome challenges and make positive choices when life feels difficult.
Empowerment – Giving children the knowledge, confidence and language to make informed decisions, ask for help when they need it and become responsible citizens.
When children leave Grafton Primary School, we hope they leave with much more than knowledge.
Above all, we hope they leave knowing that their voice matters and that they have the confidence to make a positive difference in the world around them.
We hope they understand who they are.

Centre - Afterschool Club
Centre is a place where children don't simply spend time — they grow in confidence, responsibility and kindness through the everyday experiences of being part of a community.
A happy ending to the school day
Centre is Grafton's after-school provision, offering children a safe, engaging and welcoming environment at the end of the school day.
We know that family life doesn't always finish when the school bell rings. Centre provides the reassurance that children remain in the care of familiar adults, enjoying time with friends while parents complete their working day.
After a busy day in the classroom, children have the opportunity to relax, enjoy a snack, spend time outdoors, take part in games and creative activities or simply enjoy being with their friends. Some children love organised activities, while others prefer quieter moments. We recognise that every child is different and our provision reflects this.
The atmosphere is relaxed, friendly and inclusive. Children are encouraged to make choices, develop independence and enjoy the freedom to unwind after a productive day at school.
Centre is not simply childcare — it is another opportunity for children to feel known, supported and part of our school community.
Growing Confidence and Character
Centre gives children opportunities to develop many of the personal qualities that help them flourish both in school and beyond.
Children are encouraged to take responsibility for their actions and to work through everyday disagreements with the support of caring adults. They learn how to listen to one another, solve problems respectfully and understand the importance of kindness, empathy and taking responsibility when things don't quite go to plan.
These everyday moments help children develop confidence, resilience and the social skills that underpin positive relationships throughout life.
Learning From One Another
One of the special aspects of Centre is the opportunity for children of different ages to spend time together.
Older children naturally develop leadership skills as they help and encourage younger pupils, becoming positive role models within our community. Younger children benefit from these friendships too, gaining confidence as they learn from older children in a safe and supportive environment.
These mixed-age experiences help children build respect, responsibility and a genuine sense of belonging.
Developing Independence
Children are encouraged to play an active role in the life of Centre.
Whether helping to prepare and serve snack, tidying resources, supporting younger children or taking responsibility for shared spaces, they learn that being part of a community means contributing to it.
These opportunities help children develop independence, confidence and pride in taking responsibility, while recognising that even small acts of helpfulness make a positive difference to others.
Why families value Centre
Most importantly, children leave the day feeling happy, relaxed and fulfilled.
We want children to go home happy, fulfilled and excited to come back tomorrow.
A safe and familiar environment after school
Caring staff who know the children well
Healthy refreshments
Indoor and outdoor play
Creative and social activities

Flexible support for working families
Practical Information
Payment is done via the School Money App
All parents have to complete a Registration Form for each child.
On this you indicate which days your child will attend Breakfast Club &/ Centre.
At the end of the week you are automatically charged for the sessions your child attended.
Centre Through Our Values
Love – Children continue to feel cared for long after the school day ends.
Creativity – Every afternoon offers opportunities to play, create and explore.
Kindness – Children learn to share, include one another and build positive relationships.
Inclusion – Every child is welcomed, valued and supported to enjoy their time at Centre.
Resilience – Children develop confidence, independence and problem-solving through play and shared experiences.
Empowerment – Giving children the freedom to make choices, try new activities and grow in confidence.

Our Governors
A Welcome from the Chair of Governors
Welcome to Grafton Primary School.
As Chair of Governors, it is a privilege to be part of a school community that places children at the heart of every decision it makes.
Our role as governors is to support, encourage and challenge the school's leadership so that every child receives the very best education and every family feels part of a welcoming, inclusive community. We work closely with the Headteacher and staff, celebrating the many successes of the school while providing thoughtful oversight and strategic direction for the future.
What makes Grafton so special is its unwavering belief in every child. We share that belief wholeheartedly. Whether we are discussing the curriculum, safeguarding, wellbeing, finance, the school environment or future opportunities, our focus is always the same: creating the very best experiences and outcomes for the children in our care.
Like many of my fellow governors, I have a personal connection to Grafton. As both a parent and Chair of Governors, I have seen first-hand the kindness, creativity and ambition that define this school. I am also passionate about reading and literacy, knowing the lifelong opportunities that a love of books can create for children. It is a privilege to work alongside such a dedicated team of governors, school leaders and staff, all of whom are committed to helping every child flourish.
Thank you for taking the time to find out more about us. We hope this page gives you an insight into the people who support Grafton behind the scenes and the values that guide our work.
The Role of the Governing Board
The Governing Board works in partnership with the Headteacher and senior leadership team to provide strategic leadership and accountability for the school.
Governors are not involved in the day-to-day running of Grafton. Instead, we take a longer-term view, helping to shape the school's vision, ensuring that resources are used wisely and providing both support and constructive challenge so that the school continues to grow and improve.
Together, we are responsible for:
Our governing board brings together people from a wide range of professional backgrounds, including education, law, finance, publishing, architecture, communications, local government, youth services and business. Alongside these professional skills, many governors are also current or former parents, former pupils or long-standing members of the Grafton community.
This breadth of experience allows us to ask thoughtful questions, offer informed support and ensure that decisions are always made with children's best interests at heart.
overseeing educational standards and pupil outcomes
monitoring safeguarding, wellbeing and inclusion
ensuring that financial resources are managed responsibly
Working Together
Good governance is built on collaboration.
Much of our work happens behind the scenes but rest assured that Governors meet regularly throughout the year, visiting the school, reviewing progress and working alongside school leaders. Our motivation is to support the school to provide an excellent education and inspiring, caring environment for every child.
Below you can learn more about the individuals who make up our Governing Board and the experience they bring to our school community.
Meet Our Governors
Click on the image to read more on each of our Governors
Debbie McNally
Growing up in the North East, I have now lived in London for thirty years and been part of Grafton’s parent community for nearly ten years. As Chair, I focus on strategic governance and supporting leadership to help create an environment where children can thrive academically and socially. With a background in book publishing, I am particularly passionate about literacy and reading for pleasure. Research shows that if you love to read it has a significant impact on children’s outcomes and they’ll feel the benefits for the rest of their lives.
Julian Gregory
Born and raised in Sheffield, I work as a barrister in London, primarily on group and claimant litigation. I previously stood as a Lib Dem candidate in local and national elections. My interests include public advocacy and community engagement and I bring legal, analytical and governance skills to support school leadership and strategic decision‑making. I live locally with my wife, young daughter and two cats and am an Arsenal season‑ticket holder.
Andrew Turnock
I trained as a teacher at 19 and have worked in primary and secondary settings across Leicester, Buckinghamshire and London, inspired by my mother who was a supply teacher. I bring long‑standing senior leadership experience, having been part of the SLT at Grafton for over 25 years, and I was appointed Head Teacher in 2023. I am a father of two children at Grafton, a keen cyclist, and a lifelong supporter of Wigan Athletic Football Club
Gulcin Ozdemir
I attended Grafton, as did my daughter, and I now serve as the Local Authority Governor. I am a local councillor and Chair of the Children & Young People Scrutiny Committee, and I lead work on attendance, wellbeing and educational outcomes. Alongside my council role, I’m a social work student committed to giving children the best start in life and building a safer, fairer and more inclusive borough.
Lauryn Cabey
My connection to Grafton spans 31 years as a former pupil, parent and proud member of staff. I’ve also served as Vice Chair of the PTA. I am actively involved in charity events, creative projects, performances and interventions. Extensive training in special educational needs and mental health has strengthened my commitment to inclusion and ensuring every child feels supported and valued. One project I’m especially proud of is the revival of our “Playground Friends” initiative. Grafton has shaped a huge part of who I am, and as Staff Governor I bring insight, dedication and a strong sense of community.
Alex Barros-Curtis
I am pleased to have been part of the governing board at Grafton for over ten years and served as Chair for a significant portion of that time. As an MP and the son of a schoolteacher, I value a strong academic start for every child and am proud to support school strategy here at Grafton. My experience in leadership, safeguarding and working to strengthen bonds with local communities informs my contribution.
Claire Hegarty
I was invited to join the governing body in 2020, bringing my professional background as an architect. My three now‑adult children attended Grafton and I previously served as a Parent Governor. I am vice chair of the Finance & Premises Sub‑Committee and prioritise improving the school’s buildings and learning environments. Over the years I’ve seen Grafton evolve and flourish; as a governor I want to support its creative, diverse and inclusive character and nurture strong community relations.
Graham Jimpson
I have been part of the Grafton community for 20 years, first as a parent and then as a governor, and I’ve volunteered in literacy support since 2011. My career was in youth and children’s services, with senior manager and assistant director roles across several London boroughs and contributions to national and international youth projects. Now retired, I volunteer as a mentor and trustee for local charities. I bring long experience in youth work, safeguarding and community partnership to the board. My interests include art, fell‑walking and supporting Arsenal.
Fahiimo Sharif
I am a parent of two children currently at Grafton and became a Parent Governor to represent families and strengthen communication between parents and staff. I bring a home perspective on daily school life and am committed to ensuring every child can thrive academically, socially and emotionally. I value collaboration, transparency and constructive challenge, and I work to help the governing body maintain a welcoming, ambitious and inclusive school environment.
Joanne Fowler
I am a parent of two children at Grafton and previously served as a governor at a primary school in Hackney. I have over 15 years’ experience in the education and qualifications sector and currently work as Director of Qualifications at City & Guilds, where I lead teams responsible for developing, assessing and quality‑assuring qualifications and apprenticeships. I am committed to supporting the school’s leadership through effective governance and ensuring an inclusive, high‑quality learning environment where every child feels safe.
Deb Hermer
I am an Islington parent who now has time to become more involved in the local community, having stepped down from full‑time work. I have a background in communications and project management and have supported community groups across the borough, including food banks, reading initiatives and play schemes. I joined Grafton as a governor in 2024 and am dedicated to supporting the school, beginning with the new playground project.
Ellie Prasad
I have a background in commercial project management within the British luxury fashion industry and now work freelance in creative content, communications and social media for arts and cultural organisations. As a local parent and Islington Parent Champion for Bright Start / Bright Futures, I am committed to supporting families and promoting positive early learning experiences. I bring strategic, organisational and communication skills to governance and a passion for inclusive, engaging approaches that build children’s confidence and curiosity.
Kevin Jordan
I have two children at Grafton and have lived near the school for 20 years. I am a solicitor, a local landlord and run an e‑learning community site for infrastructure finance and development. I’ve also worked as a partner in international law firms. I hope to share my business and legal experience for the benefit of the school and to contribute to the continued success of our children’s education and school experience.
Simon Chase
I worked for 15 years in the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office as a diplomat, with postings in Africa and the Middle East and London roles on Afghanistan and regional peace and security. Before that I worked in the third sector on human rights in Southern Africa. I am now a director at a global strategic advisory firm. I studied modern languages and have a passion for language learning and international education. I am the parent of three children at Grafton and support global and multilingual perspectives in school life.
Michael Tofi Associate Member
Michael Tofi
I have a long connection with Grafton, having worked at the school as a teaching assistant and been placed there during my teacher training over ten years ago. I was pleased to be appointed as an Associate Member so I could give back to the local school that helped me decide to become a teacher. I currently work for an academy trust and have held leadership roles in London and Suffolk, most recently as Assistant Headteacher, Deputy Headteacher and Associate School Lead
Jet Lim Associate Member
Jet Lim
I work as an auditor at KPMG and was inspired by my firm’s partnership with Governors for Schools to join the board at Grafton. I took on the role to better understand the challenges of running a school and to offer my support. I provide financial and analytical assistance and practical spreadsheet skills to help the school make informed decisions. I enjoy specialty coffee, ice hockey and the gym, and I hope to bring the same dedication to this role.

Breakfast Club
Giving children time to arrive before they arrive.
A calm, happy start to the day
Mornings can be busy and every family has different routines. Our Breakfast Club provides a warm, welcoming environment where children can begin the day feeling settled, nourished and ready to learn.Whether your family needs regular childcare before school or occasional support, Breakfast Club offers children a relaxed start to the morning in the company of familiar staff and friends.
Children enjoy a healthy breakfast before spending time playing, chatting, reading or taking part in activities together. There is space to socialise, laugh and ease gently into the school day, helping children arrive in class feeling calm, confident and ready to learn.
For many children, Breakfast Club becomes much more than somewhere to eat breakfast. It is a place where friendships are strengthened, confidence grows and every child feels welcomed as part of the Grafton community.
Why families value Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club provides:
Parents can leave for work knowing their children are happy, well cared for and beginning their day in a familiar environment with adults who know them well.
Time to play, socialise and build friendships
A calm transition into school
Flexible support for busy family life
Practical Information
Breakfast is served until 8:30am
Payment is via the School Money App (link)
All parents have to complete a Registration Form for each child.
On this you indicate which days your child will attend Breakfast Club &/ Centre.
At the end of the week you are automatically charged for the sessions your child attended.
All questions regarding Breakfast Club can be directed to our Extend Day Manager, Ed Fairbrother – ed.fairbrother@grafton.islington.sch.uk
Breakfast Club Through Our Values
Love – Every child is welcomed warmly and begins the day feeling cared for.
Creativity – Children have opportunities to explore activities, games and imaginative play before lessons begin.
Kindness – Friendships flourish as children spend relaxed time together in a supportive environment.
Inclusion – Every child is welcomed and encouraged to feel part of the Grafton community.
Resilience – A calm, positive start helps children feel emotionally ready for the day ahead.
Empowerment – Children develop independence, confidence and positive routines that support successful learning.

MFL - Spanish
Growing up speaking both English and Spanish has shown me how powerful language can be. It doesn't just help us communicate — it helps us understand people, cultures and different ways of seeing the world.
Subject Lead, Daniella Lopez Halil
At Grafton Primary School, we believe that learning another language opens the door to the wider world.
Spanish is much more than learning new words or phrases. It is an opportunity for children to communicate with confidence, explore different cultures and traditions, and develop an appreciation of the rich diversity of the world around them.
We want every child to leave Grafton as a confident, curious and enthusiastic linguist — someone who understands that language has the power to connect people, build friendships and open new opportunities throughout life.
Learning a Language, Growing in Confidence
Learning a new language can feel exciting, challenging and sometimes a little daunting. At Grafton, we create an environment where children feel confident to have a go, knowing that making mistakes is an important part of learning. We celebrate effort before perfection, encouraging every child to speak, listen and communicate with growing confidence.
As children's vocabulary develops, so does their belief in themselves.
More Than Words
Spanish lessons are vibrant, practical and full of opportunities for children to learn through songs, games, storytelling, role play, movement and conversation.
Children discover that language is something to be enjoyed.
And, almost without realising it, they begin communicating in another language.
Alongside developing speaking, listening, reading and writing skills, children also explore the geography, traditions, celebrations and everyday life of Spanish-speaking countries, helping them understand language within its cultural context.
Connecting Cultures
One of the greatest gifts language learning offers is the opportunity to see the world through someone else's eyes.
Spanish helps children develop respect for different cultures, traditions and ways of life while recognising and celebrating the diversity within our own school community. Many of our families already speak more than one language. Others encounter Spanish in their local community or while travelling with their families.
By learning another language, children begin to appreciate that communication brings people together and that every language tells a story.
Building Skills for Life
Our curriculum develops children's confidence progressively each year.
Most importantly, children develop the confidence to use language in real situations and understand that communication is about making connections rather than achieving perfection.
listen carefully and respond confidently
speak with increasing fluency
read familiar words and simple texts
write simple sentences independently
recognise patterns between languages
develop accurate pronunciation and intonation
Learning Beyond the Classroom
Spanish is celebrated across the school through cultural events, creative projects and whole-school experiences.
Children explore music, dance, food and traditions from Spanish-speaking countries, take part in World Day celebrations and Hispanic Heritage Month, and enjoy opportunities to experience language in meaningful and memorable ways.
These experiences help children recognise that language is alive — it is something people use every day to share ideas, traditions and stories.
Spanish Through Our Values
Everything we do in Spanish reflects the values that shape life at Grafton Primary School.
Love – Developing appreciation and respect for different cultures, traditions and ways of life.
Creativity – Learning through music, storytelling, role play, movement and imaginative communication.
Kindness – Supporting one another, celebrating different languages and helping everyone feel confident to participate.
Inclusion – Valuing multilingualism and recognising the many languages spoken within our school community.
Resilience – Understanding that mistakes are part of learning and developing the confidence to keep trying.
Empowerment – Giving children the skills and confidence to communicate with people from different cultures and backgrounds.
When children leave Grafton Primary School, we hope they leave with far more than a growing knowledge of Spanish.
The curiosity to learn about different cultures.

School Lunches
Lunchtime is an important part of the school day.
It is a chance for children to enjoy a healthy meal, spend time with friends and recharge before an afternoon of learning. At Grafton Primary School, we want lunchtime to be a positive, relaxed experience where children feel comfortable, well cared for and ready to make the most of the rest of their day.
We are proud to offer freshly prepared school meals that provide children with a balanced, nutritious diet while introducing them to a wide variety of flavours and ingredients.
Free School Meals for Every Child
All children attending Grafton Primary School are entitled to a free school meal, funded by Islington Council.
Although meals are free, all parents and carers must register their child. Registering helps ensure that the school receives the funding it is entitled to and allows us to provide the best possible support for all of our pupils.
Register HereIf you are unsure how to register, our school office will be happy to help.
Freshly Prepared Every Day
Our school meals are provided by Caterlink, Islington Council's catering partner.
Meals are freshly prepared using quality ingredients, with menus carefully planned to provide a healthy, balanced diet that children enjoy.
Ingredients include:
Our menus are designed to encourage children to explore new foods while ensuring there is always something familiar and enjoyable to choose from.
Red Tractor assured British meat wherever possible
Fresh seasonal fruit and vegetables
Special Diets and Allergies
We understand that some children have medical, cultural or dietary requirements.
If your child has a food allergy, intolerance or requires a special diet, please let the school know as soon as possible. We work closely with our catering provider to ensure that children can enjoy safe, suitable meals that meet their individual needs.
Our School Menu
Our menu changes regularly to reflect the seasons and to provide children with a varied and balanced choice of meals.
You can view our current school menu below.
Helping Children Develop Healthy Habits
Lunchtime is about more than eating.
It is an opportunity for children to develop independence, to practise good table manners, to make healthy choices and to enjoy conversation with friends.
Trying something new, sitting together and sharing a meal are all valuable parts of growing up and contribute to the welcoming, inclusive community that we value so highly at Grafton.

Educational Visits and Residentials
Learning Beyond Four Walls
Some lessons simply cannot be taught from a textbook.
These are the experiences that transform learning from something children hear about into something they remember.
At Grafton Primary School, educational visits and residential experiences are an integral part of our curriculum. They inspire curiosity, deepen understanding and create lasting memories that children carry with them long after they leave primary school.
Because the best learning often happens when children experience it for themselves.
Walking through the ruins of Roman London.
Exploring woodland on a residential visit.
Watching a live performance in a theatre.
Bringing Learning to Life
Every educational visit is carefully planned to support and enrich classroom learning.
Rather than seeing a visit as the end of a topic, we see it as part of a much bigger learning journey.
Visits encourage children to ask questions, make connections and see how their learning relates to the world around them.
A Journey Through Every Year
As children move through Grafton, each year brings new experiences and new adventures.
Every visit has been chosen because it adds something unique to children's understanding of the curriculum and of themselves.
The Adventure of Residential Learning
For many children, a residential visit is one of the highlights of primary school.
It may be their first time sleeping away from home. Their first experience of working together to overcome challenges. Their first opportunity to discover just how capable they are.
At Grafton, residential visits are about far more than outdoor activities.
Whether exploring the natural environment at Juniper Hall or taking part in the exciting challenges of the Year 6 residential, children return with a greater sense of confidence in themselves and appreciation for one another.
Encourage independence.
Develop resilience.
Strengthen friendships.
Create unforgettable shared memories.
Learning Through London — and Beyond
One of Grafton's greatest strengths is the rich learning environment on our doorstep.
Living in London gives our children access to world-class museums, galleries, theatres, universities and cultural institutions. We make the most of these opportunities, ensuring children regularly experience places that bring learning vividly to life.
At the same time, we know that some experiences require children to venture even further.
Residential visits, outdoor learning and educational journeys beyond the city help children develop confidence, curiosity and independence while experiencing environments that may be entirely new to them.
More Than Memories
Children often remember these experiences long after they have forgotten the details of a particular lesson. Not simply because they were enjoyable. But because they challenged them to think differently, work together, solve problems and discover new interests.
These moments become part of who children are. They shape the way they see the world — and the place they have within it.
Through Our Values
Love – Creating experiences that children remember with joy throughout their lives.
Creativity – Inspiring curiosity through first-hand experiences that bring learning to life.
Kindness – Building friendships, teamwork and shared memories through learning together.
Inclusion – Ensuring every child has access to rich educational experiences beyond the classroom.
Resilience – Developing confidence, independence and perseverance through new challenges.
Empowerment – Helping children discover that the world is full of opportunities waiting to be explored.

Music
At Grafton Primary School, music is woven into the life of our school.
It is heard in our assemblies, our classrooms, our performances and our celebrations. It brings energy to learning, creates moments of calm, builds confidence and gives every child the opportunity to express themselves in ways that words sometimes cannot.
We believe music is for everyone. Not just for the children who already play an instrument. Not just for those who love to sing. For every child.
Because music has a unique way of bringing people together.
Every Child Has a Place
One of the greatest gifts music offers is a sense of belonging.
Whether children are performing in an assembly, learning their first notes on the violin, singing alongside their classmates or simply listening carefully to a new piece of music, they are sharing an experience with others.
No one performs alone. No one is left out. Every child has the opportunity to take part, contribute and experience the joy of making music together.
Growing Musicians Year by Year
Our music curriculum is carefully planned so that children's musical understanding develops progressively throughout their time at Grafton.
From the earliest years, children begin exploring rhythm, pulse, singing and sound through playful musical experiences. As they grow, they build on these foundations, developing their ability to perform, compose, listen critically and understand musical notation with increasing confidence.
By Key Stage Two, every child learns to play the violin as part of our curriculum, giving them the opportunity to develop technical skill, musical understanding and the discipline that comes from learning an instrument together.
Each new experience builds upon the last, allowing children to revisit familiar concepts while developing increasingly sophisticated musical knowledge and confidence.
Learning to Listen
Music is not only about performing. It is also about listening.
We encourage children to become thoughtful listeners, exploring music from different cultures, traditions and time periods. They learn to notice rhythm, melody, dynamics and mood, but also to ask deeper questions.
Children quickly discover that music is something to experience, discuss and enjoy — not simply something that plays in the background.
How does this music make me feel?
What story does it tell?
Performing With Confidence
Performance is a natural part of life at Grafton.
Every child has opportunities to sing, play, perform and celebrate their learning throughout the year.
Class assemblies, singing assemblies, whole-school celebrations, concerts, performances and community events allow children to experience the excitement of sharing their talents with others.
These opportunities do far more than develop musical skills.
Beyond the Classroom
Music continues long after the lesson has ended.
Children perform at community events, visit live concerts, sing in our choir, take instrumental lessons and experience professional musicians performing in school.
These opportunities broaden children's musical horizons while helping them recognise that music belongs not only in school but throughout life.
Whether hearing a professional cellist perform in assembly, learning from visiting musicians or performing for parents and the local community, children discover that music is something to be shared.
Every Child Included
Music is one of the most inclusive subjects we teach.
Children are encouraged to have a go, to learn from mistakes and to support one another, creating an environment where confidence grows naturally and every achievement is celebrated.
Every child sings.
Every child performs.
Every child learns an instrument.
Music Through Our Values
Everything we do in music reflects the values that shape life at Grafton Primary School.
Love – Discovering the joy that music brings and sharing it with others.
Creativity – Exploring, composing, improvising and expressing ideas through performance.
Kindness – Listening to one another, encouraging others and celebrating every contribution.
Inclusion – Ensuring every child has the opportunity to sing, play, perform and belong.
Resilience – Developing confidence through practice, perseverance and performing in front of others.
Empowerment – Helping children discover their own voice and believe they have something worth sharing.
When children leave Grafton Primary School, we hope they leave with much more than musical knowledge and performance skills.
Because ultimately, music is not simply something we learn. It is something we experience, something we share and something that reminds us we belong.
The courage to express themselves.

Behaviour
Behaviour Begins with Relationships
At Grafton, we believe that positive behaviour grows from positive relationships.
Children behave well when they feel safe, understood, valued and connected to the adults around them. That is why we invest so much time in getting to know every child as an individual.
We understand that children are still learning — not only mathematics, reading and writing, but also how to manage emotions, solve problems, cope with disappointment and build healthy relationships.
Every day provides opportunities to teach these life skills. Behaviour is not simply something to be managed. It is something to be understood, guided and developed.
Every Behaviour Tells a Story
Sometimes behaviour communicates something that words cannot. A child may be –
This does not mean that inappropriate behaviour is accepted. It means we take time to understand what lies beneath it.
Our staff remain calm, listen carefully, ask thoughtful questions and help children recognise their feelings before supporting them to make better choices.
As our Positive Behaviour Policy states, behaviour is a form of communication and our role is to help children express themselves through appropriate words and actions.
Anxious.
Overwhelmed.
Frustrated.
Excited.
Finding friendships difficult.
Or simply having a hard day.
Kind and Firm
Being nurturing does not mean having low expectations.
Children need boundaries just as much as they need encouragement. At Grafton we are clear, calm and consistent.
But we also help them understand that feelings do not change expectations.
Children learn that it is okay to feel angry, frustrated or upset. It is not okay to hurt others, damage property or stop others from learning. This balance of kindness and consistency helps children develop resilience, self-control and responsibility.
We acknowledge disappointment.
We help children name their emotions.
We support them to regulate.
Teaching, Not Punishing
We see mistakes as opportunities for learning.
Whenever possible, we encourage children to reflect on what happened, think about how their actions affected others and consider what they might do differently next time.
Our Behaviour Policy describes this as "Doing it better next time" — an approach that reflects our belief that children should always be given the opportunity to learn from mistakes and make better choices.
Praise and encouragement play a much bigger role than sanctions because children thrive when success is noticed and celebrated. Rewards, positive recognition and meaningful responsibilities all help build confidence and reinforce positive choices.
A Calm Place to Learn
Visitors to Grafton often comment on the calm atmosphere around the school.
Our classrooms are purposeful places where children can concentrate, think deeply and enjoy learning.Adults model the respectful behaviour we hope to see. Children learn to listen to one another, solve disagreements respectfully and contribute positively to our community.
This calm environment is created through consistent routines, positive relationships and shared expectations rather than raised voices.
Supporting Every Child
Some children need additional support to help them regulate their emotions or manage the school day.
Where appropriate, we work closely with families, our SEND team and external professionals to develop personalised strategies that help children experience success. These approaches are carefully tailored to individual needs because equality does not always mean treating every child in exactly the same way.
Every child deserves to feel that they belong, even when they are finding things difficult.
Bullying
Bullying is never accepted at Grafton.
We teach children the difference between friendship difficulties, one-off disagreements and bullying, helping them understand that bullying involves behaviour that is deliberate, repeated and difficult to defend against.
If bullying does occur, we act quickly.
Children are listened to, supported and reassured.
Learning to Make Good Choices — Online and Offline
Positive behaviour extends beyond the classroom.
Children learn how to be respectful, responsible and safe both in person and online.
Through our curriculum, assemblies, PSHE and Computing lessons, children learn about kindness, respectful communication, digital citizenship and what to do if something online makes them feel worried or unsafe.
Online safety is treated as an integral part of safeguarding and is embedded across school life.
Working Together
Children thrive when school and home work together.
We value open, honest communication with families and believe that the strongest outcomes come when we work in partnership.
Together, we help children develop the confidence, empathy and self-discipline they need not only to succeed at school, but to become thoughtful, compassionate young people beyond Grafton.

pageCache.pageTitle: Grafton Primary School - Pastoral Care at Grafton
pageCache.text:
Pastoral Care at Grafton
Supporting Children and Families
At Grafton Primary School, we believe that children learn best when they feel happy, safe and supported. Every child is unique, and we know that there are times when children – and their families – may need a little extra help. Whatever the challenge, we are here to listen, to understand and to work alongside you.
Pastoral care is at the heart of our school community. It reflects our values of Love, Kindness, Inclusion, Resilience, Creativity and Empowerment, ensuring that every child feels seen, valued and encouraged to flourish both in and beyond the classroom.
Supporting Every Child
Our dedicated Pastoral Care Manager, Camilla Jarvis, works closely with children, families and staff to ensure that every child has the support they need to reach their full potential.
Whether a child is finding school difficult, experiencing friendship worries, struggling with confidence or facing challenges at home, Camilla provides a caring, consistent point of contact for families. She also coordinates our Early Help provision, working with parents, carers and external agencies to ensure support is available at the earliest opportunity.
Sometimes all that's needed is a listening ear, a conversation or practical advice. Whatever your concern, you are never alone – we're here to help.
Attendance and Punctuality
Every school day matters. Regular attendance helps children build friendships, develop confidence and make the most of every learning opportunity.
If attendance becomes a concern, our approach is always supportive rather than judgemental. We work in partnership with families to understand any barriers that may be affecting attendance and, together, develop practical plans that help children return to school feeling confident, settled and ready to learn.
Early Help
Sometimes families benefit from additional support during periods of change or difficulty. Early Help is about offering that support before challenges become bigger problems.
By identifying concerns early and working together, we can help children and families access the right advice, guidance and services at the right time.
Information regarding Early Help can be found here:
https://directory.islington.gov.uk/kb5/islington/directory/advice.page?id=wg15b0PyjZI
All conversations are treated with sensitivity and respect. While we always maintain confidentiality wherever possible, any concerns relating to a child's safety will be managed in line with our Safeguarding and Child Protection procedures.
We may not have all the answers, but together we can work out how to find them.
If you would like to speak with Camilla, please contact the school office to arrange a meeting. You'll also find her welcoming families at the school gates each morning and afternoon, where she's always happy to answer questions, offer reassurance or arrange a time to talk in more detail.
At Grafton Primary, we believe that supporting children means supporting families too. By working together, we can help every child feel confident, resilient and ready to thrive.

Nursery Admissions
The Beginning of Your Child's Grafton Journey
Starting nursery is a significant milestone, not only for children but for their families too. It is often a child's first experience of school, and we understand how important it is that they feel safe, happy and excited to learn.
At Grafton Primary School, our Nursery provides a nurturing, stimulating environment where children begin to develop confidence, curiosity and a love of learning through play, exploration and meaningful relationships.
We welcome applications throughout the year and are always happy to talk to families who would like to find out more about our Early Years provision.
Nursery Places for 3 and 4-Year-Olds
Our Nursery, Rainbow Class, is open Monday to Friday during term time.
We offer a range of flexible attendance options to support the needs of different families, including both 15-hour and 30-hour funded places for eligible children from the term after their third birthday.
15-Hour Provision
Families may choose from:
All children aged 3 and 4 are entitled to 15 hours of funded early education. To access this funding, parents simply need to complete the Parent Declaration Form so that we can claim funding on your behalf.
30-Hour Provision
Eligible working families may qualify for 30 hours of funded childcare.
Our full-time offer is:
All nursery places are offered during school term time only.
If you believe you may be eligible for 30 hours' funding, you will need to apply through the Government's childcare funding service. Once approved, you will receive an eligibility code which should be provided to the school when confirming your child's place.
Please note that eligibility must be reconfirmed every three months. If your eligibility changes, your funded entitlement may return to 15 hours.
Monday to Friday, 9.00am to 3.15pm
Nursery Places for 2-Year-Olds
Our 2+ provision offers younger children a warm, caring introduction to school life.
Sessions run Monday to Friday during term time.
If you would like to apply for a place or find out more about our 2+ provision, please contact the school office. We will be delighted to talk you through the application process.
Families may also be eligible for 15 hours of funded early education for two-year-olds. Please check your eligibility here.
Morning: 9.00am – 12.00pm
Afternoon: 12.30pm – 3.30pm (subject to availability)

Many families can access Government-funded childcare support.
Depending on your circumstances, this may include:
15 hours funded childcare for eligible two-year-olds

We encourage families to explore the available funding to find the option that best suits their circumstances.
Further Information
If you have any questions about Nursery admissions, funding or the different attendance options available, please don't hesitate to contact our school office. graftonschool@grafton.islington.sch.uk
Our team will be happy to answer your questions, arrange a visit where appropriate and help you understand the application process.
